papers.title: Riesz and Lusin type theorems in Choquet integral spaces: quasicontinuity and density of continuous functions for monotone measures
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of measurable functions by continuous functions, in measure and with respect to the Choquet, Sugeno and Shilkret integrals, for monotone measures on metric spaces. For every monotone measure, quasicontinuous functions are limits of continuous functions in measure and in the Sugeno integral; for unbounded Choquet integrable functions this remains true under a small-set subadditivity condition or under null-additivity. Conversely, under property [S1] and an outer smallness condition, every such limit is quasicontinuous, and examples show that neither condition can be omitted. This extends to monotone measures a classical description of the closure of continuous functions in capacitary $L^1$-spaces. We characterize the indicator functions in this closure by a symmetric approximation property of sets, and we give criteria, involving regularity and order continuity, for the density of bounded continuous functions. As applications, we show that two approximation theorems of Cao with compactly supported functions fail on spaces which are not locally compact, we prove that, for a given finite, continuous, weakly null-additive measure on a separable metric space, their conclusions for convergence in measure, for the Sugeno integral and for the Choquet integral of bounded functions hold if and only if the measure is concentrated on the set of points having a compact neighbourhood (and, under null-additivity, also for unbounded Choquet integrable functions), and we prove corrected versions on locally compact spaces; we describe the closure explicitly for possibility measures; and we give a Lebesgue-null Cantor dust which shows, for all $n\ge1$ and $0<\delta<n$, that continuous functions are not dense in the Choquet space of the dyadic Hausdorff content.

papers.title: How random are affine maps over finite cyclic groups and generalized cyclotomic permutations over finite fields?
papers.abstract: We analyze the dynamical behavior of affine permutations over the ring $\mathbb{Z}_{p^e}$ and generalized cyclotomic permutations (GCPs) over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We use the description of their functional graphs to determine two statistical parameters: the expected number of cycles and the expected length of a cycle that contains a random element. We obtain explicit closed-form expressions for both expectations and an exact reduction from GCPs to affine permutations. We compare these parameters with the corresponding expectations for random permutations, to determine how closely the cycle statistics of each family resemble those of random permutations.

papers.title: Condorcet's nontransitive dice: A minimal realization of a complete ranking profile
papers.abstract: We construct three independent finite-support random variables whose six strict ordering probabilities reproduce the complete ranking-frequency profile in a classical example of Condorcet's paradox. The construction has total support size seven, and we prove that no realization of this profile has smaller total support size. Here dice are allowed to be weighted: different outcomes need not have equal probabilities. We then formulate the realization problem for an arbitrary vector of six ordering probabilities. We distinguish constraints on the pairwise comparison probabilities from constraints on the full ranking distribution and give an example showing that pairwise feasibility is not sufficient. For the fixed interlaced supports $\{1,4,7\}$, $\{2,5,8\}$, and $\{3,6,9\}$, we derive the polynomial realization system. On the branch where the smallest outcome of the second variable has probability zero, we give a compact polynomial characterization for profiles with their first two ordering probabilities positive. This yields an explicit semialgebraic sufficient condition for the general realization problem and a rational construction, both with elementary proofs.

papers.title: Taylor coefficients and duality for finite multiple T-values
papers.abstract: We express every normalized finite multiple $T$-value of positive even depth as the coefficient of $u^{p-1}$ in an explicit iterated integral built from $du$ and $du/\sinh u$. An analogous formula for odd-depth $S$-values, combined with reversal, gives a coefficient representation of $T_p(\mathbf{s})$ for every nonempty index $\mathbf{s}$. The coefficients involved are $p$-integral without a restriction on the weight. For indices $(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})$ with $\ell+m$ odd, we obtain an explicit Bernoulli convolution. It yields a prime-by-prime proof of $T_p(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})=T_p(\ell+1,1,m+1)$ for odd $\ell$, and the corresponding identity with an $S$-value for even $\ell$, whenever $p\ge5$ and $p>\ell+m+1$. This proves the finite assertion of the first family in Cheng and Zhao's duality conjecture. We also establish uniform depth-two identities, evaluate the boundary cases, and explain the obstruction to the same termwise argument for $(\{1\}^{\ell},4,\{1\}^{m})$.

papers.title: Conjugate Power Series of Ultralogarithm Branches
papers.abstract: We investigate multivalued solutions of the transcendental ultralogarithm equation $e^{aw} = 1 + a x e^{bw}$ for arbitrary real parameters $a > b > 0$. A sector-based conjugation criterion is formulated and rigorously proved, reducing the technical two-dimensional indexing of conjugate master-series expansions inside ($|x| < R$) and outside ($|x| > R$) the disk of convergence to a unified one-dimensional branch index $n \in Z$. For integer exponents, a logarithmic analog of Vieta's theorem is established. Using multi-channel phase hodographs, we analyze branch evolution across integer, fractional, and transcendental incommensurable ($a = \pi$, $b = e$) exponents. It is demonstrated that logarithmic stratification eliminates branch cuts of fractional powers, ensuring global stability of iterative root refinement near branch points without auxiliary sheet-selection parameters. Finally, using the Sagdeev pseudopotential method in plasma physics, we confirm the continuous preservation of branch numbering in the Lambert $W$ limit and the physical invariance of the indices $n = 0$ (subsonic regime) and $n = -1$ (supersonic regime).

papers.title: Reflections on Thiele, Schur, and Continued Fractions
papers.abstract: We survey several classical continued-fraction constructions from a common point of view centered on linear-fractional transformations, interpolation, and the recurrence relations they generate. Beginning with Thiele's interpolation algorithm, we trace how similar mechanisms reappear in the Schur algorithm, Wall's continued fractions, and multipoint Nevanlinna--Pick interpolation. Particular attention is paid to the emergence of $R_{II}$-type continued fractions, which arise naturally as even parts of Thiele continued fractions, and to the associated pencils of tridiagonal matrices. A detour through Euler's continued-fraction formula illustrates how rational Nevanlinna functions lead naturally to finite $R_{II}$-pencils, while the Schur algorithm is related to Wall pencils and, through a different reorganization, to CMV matrices. We also discuss a modified Schur transformation that removes an interpolation condition at a pair of symmetric points, which leads to a linear pencil of two Hermitian tridiagonal matrices. Finally, we indicate how periodically occurring interpolation nodes at infinity convert $R_{II}$-pencils into ordinary banded matrices, suggesting a connection with GMP matrices.

papers.title: Gram's law for moving targets of the Riemann zeta-function
papers.abstract: We study the solutions of $\zeta(s)=f(s)$ for targets $f$ that grow with $|s|$, and Gram's law for them: the statement that each shifted Gram interval contains exactly one solution. The deviation from Gram's law is an integer phase-slip counter, equal up to rounding to $-\frac{1}{2}S(t;x_c)$, where $S(t;x)=\pi^{-1}\arg\zeta(x+it)$ and $x_c\approx 1/2+\log|f(it)|/\log t$ is a balance abscissa determined by the target. If $|f|\asymp t^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa>\kappa_1=0.5339\ldots$, where $\sum_p\arcsin(p^{-1/2-\kappa_1})=\pi$, and $\arg f$ converges, then every sufficiently high shifted Gram interval contains exactly one solution, which is simple; this localises the fixed points of $\zeta$. The threshold is sharp: for $f=c(-s)^{\kappa}$ with $1/2<\kappa<\kappa_1$, Gram's law fails in $\asymp T$ intervals up to height $T$, and for $0<\kappa\le 1/2$ it fails infinitely often but with density zero. In both ranges the counter has an explicit limiting distribution. For targets growing more slowly than any power, such as $\log(-s)$, the solutions lie on average $(1+o(1))\log|f(iT)|/\log T$ to the left of the critical line. If $\log|f(iT)|/\sqrt{\log\log T}\to\infty$, the proportion of solutions to the right of the line tends to $0$, whereas for fixed targets Selberg conjectured a quarter, and the counting error at the shifted Gram points is asymptotically Gaussian with variance $(8\pi^2)^{-1}\log(\log T/\log|f(iT)|)+O(1)$. For $\log(-s)$ the solutions follow neither $\theta(T)/\pi$ nor the zeros of $\zeta$. All results are unconditional; numerical computations for $\log(-s)$ illustrate how slowly they take effect.

papers.title: Theta-Eta Mellin Transforms, Shifted Reflections, and Rigorous Approximation Theory for a Variant Theta Construction
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous analytic framework for investigating a proposed functional equation associated with a variant theta construction. We prove the classical Mellin identity connecting the Jacobi kernel $1-\theta_4(0\mid ix^2)$ to the completed Dirichlet eta function, and extend its Mellin transform meromorphically to the whole plane with a single simple pole at the origin. Mellin uniqueness identifies $x^{3/8}(1-\theta_4(0\mid ix^2))$ as the unique kernel in a natural weighted $L^1$ class whose Mellin transform is the shifted completed eta function. We distinguish this Gaussian kernel from the weighted exponential series $\Theta^B(s)=\sum_{n\geq1}ne^{-ns}$, whose Mellin transform is $\Gamma(s)\zeta(s-1)$ and obeys a different, explicitly derived reflection relation. We show that every affine reflection $s\mapsto c-s$ can be generated for a shifted completed eta or zeta function by choosing the shift appropriately; consequently, the occurrence of $\tfrac14-s$ alone cannot identify the original variant with a shifted eta function. The corrected analytic product defined here is an elementary meromorphic multiplier of the completed zeta function and therefore has a precise $1-s$ functional equation. We prove an explicit eta-tail bound, a sharper alternating-tail asymptotic, a uniformly convergent Euler-transformed eta series with a geometric error bound, a uniform zeta-approximation bound away from the line $\Re s=1$, and a combined truncation estimate when both the zeta and weighted-exponential factors are truncated. We also determine the principal Laurent data and the cancellation of the gamma poles at the trivial zeta zeros for the corrected product. Reproducible high-precision experiments verify the stated error scales. The exact identification of the original variant with a shifted completed eta function remains open.

papers.title: Inequalities involving Higher Degree Polynomial Functions in $\pi(x)$
papers.abstract: Earlier research reflects that the two sides of Ramanujan's inequality for the prime-counting function \begin{align*} \pi(x)^2<\frac{ex}{\log x}\pi(x/e) \end{align*} happens to agree through four asymptotic orders. In this paper, we try to examine how this cancellation arises in higher-degree expressions and how shifts affect the size of the resulting gaps. In signed sums of equal powers of shifted prime counts, the first nonvanishing moment of the logarithmic shifts determines the leading term. A cubic comparison at five dilations exhibits four successive cancellations, leaving a gap of order $x^3/(\log x)^7$. A finite-difference argument proves its positivity for every real $x\geq e^{52}$ when the logarithmic shifts are spaced by $2$. When the shifts and nonnegative weights are fixed, the weighted Ramanujan gap retains order $x^2/(\log x)^6$. Its leading coefficient is $c^2(1+\sigma^2)$, where $c$ is the total rescaled weight and $\sigma^2$ is the weighted variance of the logarithmic shifts. We also give the explicit range $x\geq 85e$ for the logarithmically weighted five-shift inequality and determine the eventual sign of a polynomial family in every fixed integer degree $m\geq 3$. Exact counts and interval enclosures illustrate the expansions and the effect of variance at fixed rescaled weight and mean.

papers.title: Small Prime Primitive Roots in Arithmetic Progressions
papers.abstract: Let $p>1$ be a large prime number, let $q=O(\log\log p)$ and let $1\leq a<q$ be a pair of relatively prime integers. It is proved that there is a prime primitive root $u\ll (\log p)(\log \log p)^5$ such that $u\equiv a\bmod q$ in the prime finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$.

papers.title: Polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction: A unified approach with Application
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction by unifying the ideas of polynomial contraction and $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction and also provide demonstrative examples to show the effectiveness and novelty. Chiefly, we prove two fixed point results for polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction employing simulation functions. Lastly, we utilize our main result to discuss the existence and uniqueness of solution for boundary value problem with a concrete example in $L^p(0,\pi)$ under suitable assumptions.
